Vercel hiring Rich Harris to work full-time on Svelte is seen as a huge positive step for the Svelte community, with users feeling Vercel's backing could help SvelteKit catch up to Next.js in developer experience.
"This is awesome. Next.js is garbage so hopefully SvelteKit gets all the love and attention from now on."

A user predicted Vercel could become the dominant go-to platform for serverless frameworks, contrasting its smooth 'code and go' onboarding with Cloudflare's more confusing developer experience for Workers.

Some worried Vercel acquiring Svelte's creator amounted to buying up React's biggest competitor, creating a 'monopoly of rare, modern SSR frameworks' since Rich Harris didn't raise independent VC funding instead.

On Vercel's April 2026 security incident disclosure: "the only actionable advice is to 'review environment variables'... The advice should be to IMMEDIATELY rotate all passwords, access tokens... it spooks me how intentionally vague they seem to be."

"Vercel did not specify which of its systems were compromised... this is flatly unacceptable, right? This feels like Vercel is covering its own ass in favor of helping its customers understand the impact."
"There is no serious reason to use Vercel, other than for those being locked into the NextJs ecosystem and demo projects."
"This is why you pay a real provider for serious business needs, not an AWS reseller. Next.js is a fundamentally insecure framework, as server components are an anti-pattern full of magic."
"I appreciate the transparency in their disclosure so far, but it definitely makes you re-evaluate the risk profile of leaning entirely on fully managed PaaS solutions."

After the Mintlify XSS incident affecting Vercel and others, a commenter argued "Vercel (and other nodejs as a service providers) should warn customers that don't use CSP and --disallow-code-generation-from-strings that their settings should be improved."

"if you want to connect Vercel securely to a database with more than a password, you need to 'contact sales' about 'enterprise'... needing to contact sales about enterprise level deals just for basic security stuff is not the best move."
"Waking up to a 10k vercel bill is pretty common, especially when a DDoS goes undetected."
"Also checkout Dokploy. Incredible to leave Vercel." — implying satisfaction after switching away from Vercel to a self-hosted alternative.
"I dislike how Vercel and Netlify build up on AWS and then we only get JS/TS/Go, or WebAssembly gimmicks." — complaint about limited language support on Vercel's platform.
